Mutations in shared causal genes like PKD1, PKD2, GANAB, DNAJB11, ALG5, NEK8, and PRKCSH disrupt cellular homeostasis. Specifically, PKD1 and PKD2 are critical for primary cilia function, while GANAB, DNAJB11, ALG5, and PRKCSH are involved in ER-associated protein folding and quality control. NEK8 also plays a role in ciliary function. Dysregulation of these pathways converges on aberrant cystogenesis signaling, ultimately leading to the development of kidney cysts in ADPKD and liver cysts in PLD1.

partners.mechanism_chain: PKD2 (HGNC:9000) —DISRUPTS→ Glycosylation and ER-associated degradation (GO:0006490); GANAB (HGNC:27033) —DISRUPTS→ Glycosylation and ER-associated degradation (GO:0006490); Glycosylation and ER-associated degradation (GO:0006490) —INCREASES→ Misfolded glycoproteins (CHEBI:24390); Misfolded glycoproteins (CHEBI:24390) —LEADS_TO→ Polycystic kidney disease (HP:0000070); Misfolded glycoproteins (CHEBI:24390) —LEADS_TO→ Fundus albipunctatus (HP:0007639). Loss-of-function mutations in PKD2 (a component of the polycystin complex involved in ER homeostasis) and GANAB (an alpha-glucosidase essential for proper N-glycan processing) both lead to the accumulation of misfolded glycoproteins within the endoplasmic reticulum. This ER stress and subsequent activation of ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathways contributes to the polycystic kidney phenotype in ADPKD. In fundus albipunctatus, GANAB mutations directly impair the processing of visual cycle proteins, leading to the accumulation of lipidated retinal pigment epithelial cells and the characteristic white spots in the fundus.

#### 1. polycystic kidney disease 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.770)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620916)

**Proposed mechanism:** PKD2 (HGNC:9009) —DISRUPTS→ Polycystin complex assembly and function (GO:0005900); PKD1 (HGNC:9008) —DISRUPTS→ Polycystin complex assembly and function (GO:0005900); Polycystin complex assembly and function (GO:0005900) —LEADS_TO→ Cysts in kidney (HP:0000072); Polycystin complex assembly and function (GO:0005900) —LEADS_TO→ Kidney cysts (HP:0000072). Mutations in PKD2 (and PKD1) disrupt the formation and function of the polycystin complex, a critical component of the primary cilium. This disruption leads to cellular dysfunction and ultimately the development of renal cysts, manifesting as the shared phenotype of kidney cysts.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in PKD2 were found to consistently cause a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in one disease while causing loss-of-function in the other, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, the absence of renal cyst phenotypes in individuals with documented pathogenic PKD2 variants would also falsify this link. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in PKD2 with a minor allele frequency >0.01% in gnomAD populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving the polycystin complex and its disruption in PKD2 mutations can inform the development of targeted therapies for both autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and polycystic kidney disease 2, potentially by aiming to restore polycystin complex function or mitigate downstream cellular defects.
